<thought>The mass spectrum gives a molecular ion at m/z 262.099 Da, which matches the exact mass of the formula C₁₈H₁₄O₂. The IR shows a strong carbonyl stretch at ~1740 cm⁻¹ and multiple aromatic C–H stretches around 3100 cm⁻¹, indicating an aromatic carbonyl compound (likely a ketone or ester) with two aromatic rings. The most parsimonious structure that fits C₁₈H₁₄O₂, contains a carbonyl, and is fully aromatic is **benzophenone‑2‑yl‑phenyl ketone**, i.e., a diaryl ketone where one aryl ring is a phenyl and the other is a 2‑phenyl (biphenyl) moiety. This structure can be represented by the SMILES string `O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2c3ccccc3`, which corresponds to a carbonyl carbon attached to three phenyl rings (a tri‑aryl ketone) and has the exact formula C₁₈H₁₄O₂. The SMILES is valid and matches the observed data while requiring no further costly measurements.</thought>
<final_answer>O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2c3ccccc3</final_answer>
